panels.description: Projected calendar-month total from vnStat, the authoritative counter against Seedhost's 100 TB cap. Was extrapolated from node_network_*_bytes_total, which resets on every reboot (zincati reboots this box weekly) and is bounded by 14d retention, so it systematically under-reported.
panels.title: Month pace vs 100 TB cap

panels.description: Actual bytes used this calendar month, both directions, from vnStat's own database — survives reboots and Prometheus retention.
panels.title: Month to date (vnStat)

panels.description: All mdadm arrays, not just the data array. Healthy is failed=0 and spare=0 everywhere, with active equal to the member count. Arrays are deliberately NOT pinned by name: mdadm renumbered them md4 -> md125/md126/md127 at the 2026-07-20 FCOS rebuild, which is exactly what silently emptied this panel and killed SeedboxRAIDDegraded. md125 = 23.8 TB RAID5 data array, md126 = /boot, md127 = OS.
panels.title: RAID disks by state

panels.description: The old query keyed on mountpoint="/", which FCOS never reports (/ is a composefs overlay node-exporter does not surface), so this panel was permanently empty and SeedboxDiskFillHigh could never fire. /var and /var/mnt/seedbox are the real filesystems. /boot is excluded: at 367 MB the same percentage threshold is meaningless. md127 is mounted at four paths reporting identical numbers, so mountpoints are pinned rather than matched loosely.
panels.title: Filesystem usage

panels.description: Fraction of each second the disk spent doing I/O — 1.0 means saturated.
panels.title: Disk I/O per device

panels.description: Instantaneous transfer speeds reported by qBittorrent (already gauges — no rate()).
panels.title: qBittorrent up/down rate

panels.description: Overall availability. 'Box reachable' is the independent blackbox TCP probe to the public IP (true box-up, does not use the tailnet). 'Scrape path health' is the fraction of the 5 tailnet sensors up (seedbox:up:ratio). 'qBittorrent WebUI' is the qBit exporter scrape. Box reachable staying at 1 while the others dip = tailnet/qBit degradation, not an outage.
panels.title: Seedbox availability — box vs scrape path vs qBit

panels.description: Lifetime upload / download per tracker, straight from qui. Red below 1.0 — that tracker has taken more than it has given back. Aggregated by tracker_name, so no tracker is named in this repo; the panel renders whatever qBittorrent is actually seeding.
panels.title: Ratio by tracker

panels.description: How the seeding population is distributed across trackers over time. A line stepping down is a qbit-manage cull; a line at zero is a tracker that has stopped contributing entirely.
panels.title: Torrents by tracker

panels.description: Lifetime bytes uploaded per tracker. Slope is what matters — a flat line means that tracker's torrents are seeding to nobody. Resets when torrents are culled, so read the shape, not the absolute value.
panels.title: Cumulative upload by tracker

panels.description: Torrents that have uploaded nothing at all (ratio 0), and the disk they hold. This is the cull-candidate pool: on a ratio box it is pure cost. Sourced from the per-torrent metrics deliberately kept in servicemonitor.yaml.
panels.title: Dead weight

panels.description: The 20 largest torrents at ratio 0, worst first. Cross-check against the tracker's hit-and-run rules before removing anything: a recent grab may simply not have found a peer yet.
panels.title: Cull candidates — biggest torrents that have never uploaded

panels.description: The 20 torrents doing the actual work. Useful for spotting which trackers and which content types repay their disk, and therefore what is worth grabbing more of.
panels.title: Top earners — lifetime upload

panels.description: Emptying the bin frees only the reclaimable series. cross-seed hardlinks reach from the bin into the live library, so deleting the bin's copy of those inodes frees nothing — measured at roughly half the footprint. Reading du as headroom overstates it by ~2x.
panels.title: RecycleBin — reclaimable vs pinned

panels.description: The component behind the 2026-08-25 incident that left 40 torrents in missingFiles. It had no metrics at all until 2026-09-05; diagnosis was grepping the log.
panels.title: qbit-manage — culls

panels.description: Injections against the work done to get them. A high search count with near-zero injections is a tracker problem, not a cross-seed one. Sustained auth failures mean a tracker session has expired.
panels.title: cross-seed — yield and failures

panels.description: qBittorrent 5 keeps torrent metadata only in torrents.db. This is the format-independent copy that makes a corrupt database recoverable. 'uncovered' above zero means a torrent has no exported .torrent.
panels.title: Torrent metadata backup

panels.description: `issue` is applied when a tracker errors and rises before any ratio moves, so it is the earliest warning that a tracker is going bad.
panels.title: Torrents by qbit-manage tag

panels.description: Per-indexer traffic from Prowlarr's own stats endpoint, which nothing collected before 2026-09-05. Queries with no grabs behind them is the shape to look for: it means an indexer is being asked and returning nothing usable, so it costs announce budget and yields no ratio. Counters start at zero when the exporter restarts, hence rate() rather than the raw totals.
panels.title: Prowlarr — indexer queries and grabs

panels.description: Failures split by kind, because they mean different things. A failed AUTH query is a credential or session problem and is never normal; a failed query is usually the tracker being flaky. Response time is the third signal: an indexer that is slow but succeeding still eats the search window that cross-seed runs in.
panels.title: Prowlarr — indexer failures and latency
